title: The triterpenoid ursolic acid ameliorates stress in Caenorhabditis elegans by affecting the depression-associated genes skn-1 and prdx2.
authors: Nass, Janine; Abdelfatah, Sara; Efferth, Thomas
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究熊果酸通过影响skn-1和prdx2基因缓解线虫应激，涉及分子对接但核心是抗氧化与抑郁关联，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，方法仅简单对接，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Depression is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. Lower antioxidant concentrations and increased oxidative stress levels contribute to the development of depression. Effective and tolerable medications are urgently needed. Nrf2 and PRDX2 are promising targets in the treatment of oxidative stress and, therefore, promising for the development of novel antidepressants. Ursolic acid (UA), a natural triterpenoid found in various plants is known to exert neuroprotective and antioxidant effects. Skn-1 (which corresponds to human Nrf2) and prdx2 deficient mutants of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans are suitable models to study the effect of UA on these targets. Additionally, stress assays are used to mimic stress or depressed state. METHODS: We examined the antioxidant activity of UA in Caenorhabditis elegans wildtype and skn-1- and prdx2-deficient strains by H(2)DCF-DA and juglone assays as well as osmotic and heat stress assays. Additionally, we analyzed the binding of UA to human PRDX2 and Skn-1 proteins by molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis. RESULTS: UA exerted strong antioxidant activities. Additionally, induction of stress resistance towards osmotic and heat stress was observed. qRT-PCR revealed that UA upregulated the gene expression of skn-1 and prdx2. Molecular docking studies supported these findings. CONCLUSION: Our findings implicate that the strong antioxidant activity of UA may exert anti-depressive effects by its interaction with the Skn-1 transcription factor, which is part of a detoxification network, and the antioxidant PRDX2 protein, which protects the organism from the detrimental effects of radical oxygen species.
abstract_zh: 引言：抑郁症是全球范围内导致死亡的主要原因之一。较低的抗氧化剂浓度和增加的氧化应激水平促进了抑郁症的发展。迫切需要有效且耐受性良好的药物。Nrf2和PRDX2是治疗氧化应激的有前景靶点，因此也适合开发新型抗抑郁药。熊果酸（UA）是一种存在于多种植物中的天然三萜类化合物，已知具有神经保护和抗氧化作用。线虫（Caenorhabditis elegans）的Skn-1（对应人类Nrf2）和prdx2缺陷突变体是研究UA对这些靶点作用的合适模型。此外，应激实验用于模拟应激或抑郁状态。方法：我们通过H(2)DCF-DA和胡桃醌实验以及渗透压和热应激实验，检测了UA在野生型、skn-1和prdx2缺陷型线虫中的抗氧化活性。此外，我们通过分子对接和微量热泳动分析了UA与人类PRDX2和Skn-1蛋白的结合。结果：UA表现出强抗氧化活性。此外，观察到对渗透压和热应激的应激抵抗性诱导。qRT-PCR显示UA上调了skn-1和prdx2的基因表达。分子对接研究支持了这些发现。结论：我们的发现表明，UA的强抗氧化活性可能通过与Skn-1转录因子（解毒网络的一部分）和抗氧化蛋白PRDX2（保护生物体免受活性氧物种有害影响）的相互作用发挥抗抑郁效应。
